before.title: The retarded wave kernel is a distribution supported on the cone, solves the point-wave equation, and convolves to the retarded solution
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), used through the sphere and polar integrations below ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]). Let $c>0$, write $Q:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $\mathcal D:=\mathcal D(Q)$ for the test-function space of [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], and $C:=\{(y,t)\in Q:t=|y|/c\}$ for the retarded cone. Define the functional $K$ on test functions by $$\langle K,\psi\rangle:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\psi(y,|y|/c)}{|y|}\,dy\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal D).$$ Then: (a) the integral converges absolutely for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$, the functional $K$ is a distribution on $Q$ ([[def-distribution]]), $(K,\psi)=0$ for every $\psi$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap C=\varnothing$, and for every $(y_0,t_0)\in C$ and every neighbourhood $U$ of $(y_0,t_0)$ there is $\psi\in\mathcal D$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\subseteq U$ and $\langle K,\psi\rangle\ne0$; consequently $\operatorname{supp}K=C$. (b) For every $h\in C_c^\infty(Q)$ the function $$(K*h)(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{h(y,\,t-|x-y|/c)}{4\pi\,|x-y|}\,dy$$ is well defined (the integral converges absolutely), of class $C^\infty$ on $Q$, and for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$ $$\langle K*h,\psi\rangle=\langle h,\,K\circledast\psi\rangle,\qquad (K\circledast\psi)(y,s):=\langle K,\psi(y+\cdot,s+\cdot)\rangle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int\frac{\psi(y+z,s+|z|/c)}{|z|}\,dz;$$ moreover $W(K*h)=h$ on $Q$ in the classical pointwise sense, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ is the wave expression of [[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]] and [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. (c) Read $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ as the distributional operator built from [[def-distributional-derivative]]; then $WK=\delta_{(0,0)}$ in the sense of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]], that is, $(WK)(\psi)=\psi(0,0)$ for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$. This identifies $K$ as the retarded fundamental solution of $W$; no smoothness of $K$ itself on the cone is asserted, and the advanced fundamental solution is not treated.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) Well-definedness and continuity: fix $\psi\in\mathcal D$ with support in a compact set, choose $R>0$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\subseteq B_R(0)\times[-R,R]$ ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]]), and let $M:=\sup|\psi|<\infty$ on the compact support ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]). Then $|\langle K,\psi\rangle|\le\frac{M}{4\pi}\int_{B_R}|y|^{-1}dy$ ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]), and by [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] applied to the nonnegative Borel function $y\mapsto|y|^{-1}\mathbf 1_{B_R}(y)$, with $d\sigma$ the polar measure of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], $\int_{B_R}|y|^{-1}dy=\int_0^Rr^{-1}\sigma(S^2)r^2\,dr=\tfrac12\sigma(S^2)R^2<\infty$. Hence the integral converges absolutely and the bound is a fixed-support seminorm of [[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]] on each $\mathcal D_K$, i.e. $K$ is continuous for the LF topology of [[def-test-function-topology]]: $K\in\mathcal D'$. Support: if $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap C=\varnothing$ then $\psi(y,|y|/c)=0$ for every $y\ne0$, so the integrand vanishes off the null set $\{0\}$ and $\langle K,\psi\rangle=0$. Conversely fix $(y_0,t_0)\in C$ and a neighbourhood $U$. If $y_0\ne0$, take a nonnegative bump $\psi$ supported in a small ball inside $U$ about $(y_0,t_0)$ with $\psi(y_0,t_0)>0$: by continuity $\psi(\cdot,|\cdot|/c)$ is positive on a neighbourhood of $y_0$, a set of positive measure, and $|y|^{-1}$ is bounded there, so $\langle K,\psi\rangle>0$ ([[thm-nonnegative-integral-zero-iff-zero-almost-everywhere]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]]). If $y_0=0$, then $t_0=0$ and $\psi(y,t)=\rho(|y|)\eta(t)$ with nonnegative bump factors supported in a small ball about the origin inside $U$ and positive at the origin gives $\langle K,\psi\rangle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int\rho(|y|)\eta(|y|/c)|y|^{-1}dy>0$ by the same positivity argument. Hence no point of $C$ is outside the support and $\operatorname{supp}K=C$. (b) For fixed $(x,t)$ the defining integral converges absolutely: if $\operatorname{supp}h\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)\times[-\rho,\rho]$ and $(y,t-|x-y|/c)\in\operatorname{supp}h$, then $y\in\overline B_{\rho+|x|}(0)$; $|h|\le\|h\|_\infty$ and $1/(4\pi|x-y|)$ is integrable over that compact ball by the same polar computation, so [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]] gives absolute convergence. Pairing identity: substitute $x=y+z$ in the $x$-integral and $t=s+|z|/c$ in the $t$-integral (two translations of Lebesgue measure, [[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]) and interchange the $y$- and $(z,t)$-integrations with [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] (the integrand is continuous on the compact product of the supports): $\langle K*h,\psi\rangle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int h(y,s)\Bigl[\int\frac{\psi(y+z,s+|z|/c)}{|z|}dz\Bigr]dyds=\langle h,K\circledast\psi\rangle$, the inner bracket being exactly the definition of $K$ applied to the test function $(z,u)\mapsto\psi(y+z,s+u)$ (its support is compact). Identification with the wave solution: let $h\in C_c^\infty(Q)$ and $t_0$ below the time support of $h$. Apply [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] with $a=b=0$ and source $h$ on the slab $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$, $T$ above the time support: its solution is $u(x,t)=c^2\int_{t_0}^tH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$ with $H_\varphi(x,s)=sM_{cs}\varphi(x)$, $M_{r}\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}\varphi(x+rn)\,d\Omega(n)$. Writing the sphere average as an integral over the sphere and using [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]] on the compact rectangle $[t_0,t]\times S^2$, the substitution $r=c(t-v)$ with the absolute derivative ([[cor-one-dimensional-change-of-variables-with-absolute-derivative]]) turns the integral into $u(x,t)=\int_0^{c(t-t_0)}r\,\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+rn,t-r/c)\,d\Omega(n)\,dr$. The chart surface measure on $S^2$ agrees with the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]], $n=3$), so applying [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]] to the nonnegative Borel function $y\mapsto|h(x+y,t-|y|/c)|(4\pi|y|)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{|y|\le c(t-t_0)}$ (and passing to positive and negative parts, [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]) gives $u(x,t)=\int_{|y|\le c(t-t_0)}\frac{h(x+y,\,t-|y|/c)}{4\pi|y|}\,dy$; the omitted range $|y|>c(t-t_0)$ has $t-|y|/c<t_0$, where $h=0$. After the reflection $y\mapsto-y$ this is $(K*h)(x,t)$ on the whole slab. Since for every point $(x_*,t_*)\in Q$ one can choose a slab $[t_0,T]$ containing it with $t_0$ below and $T$ above the time support of $h$, [[thm-em-wave-cauchy-kirchhoff]] gives $Wu=h$ at that point and $K*h=u$ there; hence $K*h$ (well defined on all of $Q$ and smooth on every slab) is $C^\infty$ on $Q$ and $W(K*h)=h$ pointwise. (c) Let $\eta\in C_c^\infty(Q)$ be a nonnegative bump with $\int\eta=1$ and $\operatorname{supp}\eta\subseteq\overline B_1(0)$ and let $\eta_\varepsilon$ be its mollifier family ([[def-mollifier-family-generated-by-a-unit-mass-smooth-bump]], [[def-l-one-approximate-identity-on-rn]]). By (b), $W(K*\eta_\varepsilon)=\eta_\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. For bounded continuous $\varphi$, $\langle\eta_\varepsilon,\varphi\rangle\to\varphi(0)$: convolve with the reflected bump and apply [[cor-l-one-approximate-identities-converge-uniformly-on-compacta-for-continuous-functions]] at the origin. Hence for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$, $\langle K*\eta_\varepsilon,\psi\rangle=\langle\eta_\varepsilon,K\circledast\psi\rangle\to(K\circledast\psi)(0,0)=\langle K,\psi\rangle$, because $K\circledast\psi$ is continuous (its defining integral is dominated by $2\|\psi\|_\infty/(4\pi|z|)$ on a compact $z$-set, so [[thm-dominated-convergence]] applies as $(y,s)\to(0,0)$), i.e. $K*\eta_\varepsilon\to K$ in the weak topology of $\mathcal D'$. The distributional operator $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ is a continuous linear map on $\mathcal D'$ for the weak topology, being a finite linear combination of derivatives, each of which is continuous linear ([[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); therefore $WK=W(\lim_\varepsilon K*\eta_\varepsilon)=\lim_\varepsilon W(K*\eta_\varepsilon)=\lim_\varepsilon\eta_\varepsilon=\delta_{(0,0)}$ in $\mathcal D'$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]). No smoothness of $K$ on the cone is claimed or used.

used_after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), used through the sphere and polar integrations below ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]], [[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]]). Let $c>0$, write $Q:=\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, $\mathcal D:=\mathcal D(Q)$ for the test-function space of [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], and $C:=\{(y,t)\in Q:t=|y|/c\}$ for the retarded cone. Define the functional $K$ on test functions by $$\langle K,\psi\rangle:=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\psi(y,|y|/c)}{|y|}\,dy\qquad(\psi\in\mathcal D).$$ Then: (a) the integral converges absolutely for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$, the functional $K$ is a distribution on $Q$ ([[def-distribution]]), $(K,\psi)=0$ for every $\psi$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\cap C=\varnothing$, and for every $(y_0,t_0)\in C$ and every neighbourhood $U$ of $(y_0,t_0)$ there is $\psi\in\mathcal D$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\subseteq U$ and $\langle K,\psi\rangle\ne0$; consequently $\operatorname{supp}K=C$. (b) For every $h\in C_c^\infty(Q)$ the function $$(K*h)(x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{h(y,\,t-|x-y|/c)}{4\pi\,|x-y|}\,dy$$ is well defined (the integral converges absolutely), of class $C^\infty$ on $Q$, and for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$ $$\langle K*h,\psi\rangle=\langle h,\,K\circledast\psi\rangle,\qquad (K\circledast\psi)(y,s):=\langle K,\psi(y+\cdot,s+\cdot)\rangle=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int\frac{\psi(y+z,s+|z|/c)}{|z|}\,dz;$$ moreover $W(K*h)=h$ on $Q$ in the classical pointwise sense, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ is the wave expression of [[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]] and [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]. (c) Read $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$ as the distributional operator built from [[def-distributional-derivative]]; then $WK=\delta_{(0,0)}$ in the sense of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]], that is, $(WK)(\psi)=\psi(0,0)$ for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$. This identifies $K$ as the retarded fundamental solution of $W$; no smoothness of $K$ itself on the cone is asserted, and the advanced fundamental solution is not treated.

(a) Well-definedness and continuity: fix $\psi\in\mathcal D$ with support in a compact set, choose $R>0$ with $\operatorname{supp}\psi\subseteq B_R(0)\times[-R,R]$ ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]]), and let $M:=\sup|\psi|<\infty$ on the compact support ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]). Hence the integral converges absolutely and the bound is a fixed-support seminorm of [[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]] on each $\mathcal D_K$, i.e. $K$ is continuous for the LF topology of [[def-test-function-topology]]: $K\in\mathcal D'$. For the approximate-identity application in (c), F(y,s)=(K circledast psi)(y,s) is bounded on ALL parameter space: if the spatial projection of supp psi lies in B_M with M>0, the contributing z lie in B_M-y. For |y|<=2M this is contained in B_3M and its |z|^-1 integral is finite; for |y|>2M one has |z|>=|y|-M>M and the integral is bounded by |B_M|/M. Multiply by ||psi||infinity/(4pi). Continuity on every bounded parameter neighborhood follows from the same fixed compact-z polar majorant and dominated convergence. Thus the stated bounded-continuous approximate-identity interface is actually applicable.

before.title: Zonal and quadratic sphere moments for the polar surface measure on $S^2$
before.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the dipole and emitted-power items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-36.notes.md)
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), as carried by the surface-measure interface below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), let $e_3$ be the third vector of the standard basis and write $n_3=n\cdot e_3$ for $n\in S^2$. Then: (a) [Zonal identity] for every continuous $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$, $$\int_{S^2}f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du.$$ (b) [Linear weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)\,f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3\int_{-1}^{1}u\,f(u)\,du.$$ (c) [Quadratic weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3^{2}\int_{-1}^{1}u^{2}f(u)\,du+\pi\,(a_1^{2}+a_2^{2})\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})f(u)\,du.$$ (d) [Moments] $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, $\int_{S^2}n\,d\sigma=0$, $\int_{S^2}n_in_j\,d\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$, and for every $a\in\mathbb R^3$ $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$ and $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker symbol and $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) [Scope] (a)-(d) are identities for the polar surface measure of the unit sphere with only the stated continuity of $f$; they assert no physical field, flux or radiation statement. The measure is finite, so all displayed integrals are absolutely convergent; $f$ need not be nonnegative. For the uses on this page $f$ is a rational function with denominator bounded below by $1-b>0$, hence continuous on $[-1,1]$.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) Parametrize $S^2$ by $X(\theta,\varphi):=(\sin\theta\cos\varphi,\ \sin\theta\sin\varphi,\ \cos\theta)$ on $[0,\pi]\times[0,2\pi]$. Computing the coordinate cross product with the sin/cos derivatives and the Pythagorean identity ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]], [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]) gives $X_\theta\times X_\varphi=\sin\theta\,X(\theta,\varphi)$, whose norm is $\sin\theta\ge0$; by [[thm-surface-area-density-is-cross-product-norm]] and [[def-surface-area-and-scalar-surface-integral-of-a-patch]] the chart surface integral of $F(n)=f(n_3)$ is $\int_0^{2\pi}\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta\,d\varphi$, with the seam and the poles lying on the parameter boundary exactly as in the sphere-area computation, so this is the integral over $S^2$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-parameter-boundary-exceptions-do-not-affect-surface-integrals|the boundary-exception convention]]). The chart measure equals the polar measure $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). By [[thm-jordan-fubini-by-sections]] the $\varphi$-integral is the constant $2\pi$, and with $P(u):=\int_0^u f$ ([[thm-ftc-first-part]]) the chain rule and [[thm-ftc-second-part]] give $\int_0^{\pi}f(\cos\theta)\sin\theta\,d\theta=[-P(\cos\theta)]_0^{\pi}=P(1)-P(-1)=\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du$, using $\cos0=1$, $\cos\pi=-1$ and the derivative $\cos'=-\sin$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]). This proves (a), including the endpoint values by continuity of $P\circ\cos$ on $[0,\pi]$ and the two-sided fundamental theorem. (b) Write $n\cdot a=a_1n_1+a_2n_2+a_3n_3$. The maps $\eta_1(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(-n_1,n_2,n_3)$ and $\eta_2(n_1,n_2,n_3):=(n_1,-n_2,n_3)$ are orthogonal and preserve $\sigma$ ([[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); since $n_1f(n_3)$ and $n_2f(n_3)$ change sign under $\eta_1$ and $\eta_2$ respectively, the substitution formula for the measure-preserving involution $\eta_i$ (indicators by definition, simple functions by linearity, bounded Borel functions by the usual approximation, exactly as in the vanishing-first-moment computation of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]) gives $\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=-\int n_if(n_3)d\sigma=0$ for $i=1,2$; the remaining term is $a_3\int n_3f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi a_3\int_{-1}^1uf(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=uf(u)$. (c) Expanding the square, the mixed terms $n_in_jf(n_3)$ with $i\ne j$ vanish by the same reflection argument; the terms $n_1^2$ and $n_2^2$ are equal by the swap $(n_1,n_2,n_3)\mapsto(n_2,n_1,n_3)$, which is orthogonal and preserves $\sigma$. Hence $\int n_1^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\int n_2^2f(n_3)d\sigma=\tfrac12\int(1-n_3^2)f(n_3)d\sigma=\pi\int_{-1}^1(1-u^2)f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=(1-u^2)f(u)$, while $\int n_3^2f(n_3)d\sigma=2\pi\int_{-1}^1u^2f(u)du$ by (a) applied to $F(u)=u^2f(u)$; linearity of the $\sigma$-integral on the (finite-measure) integrable functions is [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]. This proves (c). (d) Taking $f=1$ in (a) gives $\sigma(S^2)=2\pi\cdot2=4\pi$, which also evaluates the closed form of [[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]] at $n=3$ together with the Gamma values $\Gamma(5/2)=(3/2)(1/2)\Gamma(1/2)=3\sqrt\pi/4$ ([[thm-real-gamma-functional-equation]], [[cor-real-gamma-one-half-is-root-pi]]), so the two routes agree. Taking $f=1$ in (b),(c) gives $\int n_if(n_3)=0$ for $i=1,2$ and the matrix identity $\int n_in_jd\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$ (equivalently $\int(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$); the first moment statement is the three-dimensional case of [[lem-first-moment-of-the-unit-sphere-vanishes]]. used_after.reference: scaffold-added necessary mathematical prerequisite for the dipole and emitted-power items (see research/physics-em-sr-40-2026-10-08-batch-36.notes.md)
used_after.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), as carried by the surface-measure interface below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\sigma$ be the polar surface measure on the unit sphere $S^2\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]), let $e_3:=(0,0,1)$ be the third coordinate unit vector and write $n_3=n\cdot e_3$ for $n\in S^2$. Then: (a) [Zonal identity] for every continuous $f:[-1,1]\to\mathbb R$, $$\int_{S^2}f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\int_{-1}^{1}f(u)\,du.$$ (b) [Linear weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)\,f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3\int_{-1}^{1}u\,f(u)\,du.$$ (c) [Quadratic weighted moment] for every continuous $f$ and every $a\in\mathbb R^3$, $$\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2f(n_3)\,d\sigma(n)=2\pi\,a_3^{2}\int_{-1}^{1}u^{2}f(u)\,du+\pi\,(a_1^{2}+a_2^{2})\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})f(u)\,du.$$ (d) [Moments] $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$, $\int_{S^2}n\,d\sigma=0$, $\int_{S^2}n_in_j\,d\sigma=(4\pi/3)\delta_{ij}$, and for every $a\in\mathbb R^3$ $\int_{S^2}(n\cdot a)^2d\sigma=(4\pi/3)|a|^2$ and $\int_{S^2}|n\times a|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|a|^2$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is the Kronecker symbol and $\times$ the cross product of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]. (e) [Scope] (a)-(d) are identities for the polar surface measure of the unit sphere with only the stated continuity of $f$; they assert no physical field, flux or radiation statement. The measure is finite, so all displayed integrals are absolutely convergent; $f$ need not be nonnegative. For the uses on this page $f$ is a rational function with denominator bounded below by $1-b>0$, hence continuous on $[-1,1]$.

before.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) as carried by the declared distributional/surface source objects of [[def-em-weak-sources]]. In the flat classical laboratory model of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the positive constants and SI conventions of [[def-em-si-conventions]], adopt the following additional physical assumption for models using the declared point or stationary-sheet sources: the locally integrable field pair and the volume-plus-singular source pair of [[def-em-weak-sources]](a)-(d) must satisfy its solution predicate (e). Explicitly,
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad\operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
are required in $\mathcal D'(U)$, meaning that all four residual pairings defined there vanish for every compact smooth test. This is a physical adoption of the classical vacuum idealization in that source class, not a theorem about sources or a consequence of the original locally-integrable-source branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]. When the singular part vanishes, the adopted identities coincide with that earlier weak branch.
Only source/field tuples satisfying these identities are models of this postulate; it does not assert existence for every prescribed source pair, and compatibility conditions remain consequences to be checked. Sources are the exact point and stationary-sheet types defined earlier, including their properness/endpoint and tangential-current qualifications. No moving sheet, line current, magnetic source, product of distributions, self-force, regularization, matter dynamics or material constitutive law is introduced. This postulate reports no experiment or measurement and does not infer empirical certainty from its mathematical formulation.
before.strategy: Nonproof formulation and scope review: adopt the already-defined four residual identities for the specified classical point/sheet source idealizations. Textbook point-delta and sheet-delta Maxwell treatments support this model choice; the exact compact-test formulation is supplied by the preceding definition. This is an explicit further physical premise, not an application of the old L1-only postulate outside its domain and not a fabricated deductive proof. The consistency/continuity and jump consequences belong to consuming conditional theorems.

before.title: The Lorentz coupling: external force on a test charge and the continuum force and power densities
before.statement:
Adopt as physical postulates of this framework, on the spacetime and particle model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] and on the special-relativity particle model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: (i) [Test charge in a prescribed external field] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter ([[def-em-sources]]), $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass, $x:J\to A$ a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline with four-velocity $U$, and let $F$ be a prescribed field of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle. Adopt the equation of motion

$$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),$$

where $\Phi$ is the raised-index operator of the field at the event $x(\tau)$, defined by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]); equivalently $m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=q\,F^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$. The particle's own field is excluded from $F$: this is the external-field coupling, and it defines no self-force. (ii) [Continuum matter coupling] For a smooth source $(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] interacting with the field through an explicitly stated matter model to which this coupling applies, adopt the force density $\rho E+J\times B$ (unit N m$^{-3}$) and the power density $J\cdot E$ (unit W m$^{-3}$) as the electromagnetic source terms of that matter model; they describe the local interaction of the field with matter and are not a property of a prescribed current alone. (iii) [Scope] The rest mass and the charge are inputs; $m$ is not derived within electromagnetism. The coupling is adopted for constant $q$ and $m>0$; no magnetic-monopole coupling, no radiation reaction and no self-force are included. In particular the nonrelativistic coordinate statement $mr''=q(E+r'\times B)$ is not adopted as exact: the adopted statement is the covariant one of clause (i), and any low-speed statement requires its own approximation hypotheses and error bounds.
before.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. The exposition must state the exact data (constant charge, externally supplied positive rest mass, future timelike C^2 worldline, prescribed external field C^1 near the graph), name the raised-index operator $\Phi$ with its defining identity and index form from [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] so that the equation is unambiguous, and state the exclusion of the particle's own field. Clause (ii) is a formulation premise for matter models, with its units fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]] and its cross product the spatial one of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; it is not a derivation from the field equations. Clause (iii) records the scope: no self-force, no radiation reaction, no magnetic monopole, and no exact Newtonian law. Empirical support for the coupling is a nonlogical relation of the framework; the item claims no verification and no measured value.

before.statement: Adopt as a physical assumption of this framework the following solution-selection rule for the classical vacuum model on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the constants and SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]] (so $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$). (a) [Formulation] In the potential formulation of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]] with the conventions of [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], for a $C^2$ potential pair in Lorenz gauge the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] is equivalent to the decoupled sourced wave equations $W\varphi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $WA=\mu_0J$, where $W=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$. The wave expression $W$ is invariant under $t\mapsto-t$; consequently, for a prescribed source history, the solution set of the sourced wave equations consists of one retarded branch (built from the retarded fundamental solution, support in the forward light cones) and one advanced branch, and the difference of any two solutions with the same source is a free field, i.e. a source-free solution of $W$. (b) [Adopted rule] The framework adopts the retarded branch with no free field added: the physical potential pair of the model is the retarded one, that is, the one whose support and propagation lie in the forward light cones of the source and which carries no field arriving from the past independently of the source. Equivalently: on any region for which initial data are prescribed on a spacelike Cauchy surface, the rule is that the homogeneous addition is exactly the one determined by those data, with zero incoming radiation; the advanced branch and every nonzero free field are excluded from the physical solution of this model. (c) [Status and scope] This is an adopted extra temporal condition carrying the model's arrow-of-time content. It is not a theorem, not a consequence of the time-symmetric wave or Maxwell equations (which admit advanced and free solutions as mathematical objects), and not a deduction from experiment; it asserts no existence, uniqueness, regularity, support or decay for any source class, all of which must be supplied separately by theorems of this page. It selects a solution only of the models to which it is applied; it introduces no product of distributions, no source model, no self-force, no radiation reaction, no measured signal and no statistical claim. The retarded compact-source branch to which this selection applies is developed on this page as a conditional theorem, and the point-source branch is developed later on this page; neither existence statement is part of this postulate.
before.strategy: A postulate: the item records an adopted solution-selection rule, and receives a source/scope review rather than a proof. The review checks that (i) the formulation correctly displays the wave expression $W$, its time-reversal symmetry, the retarded and advanced fundamental-solution branches and the free-field freedom, all with the exact interfaces of [[pthm-em-lorenz-gauge-wave-form]], [[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]] and [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; (ii) the adopted rule is stated as a modelling choice with its arrow-of-time content, and is not presented as a consequence of the equations; (iii) the formulation does not pretend to prove existence or uniqueness for any source class and expressly defers those to the consuming theorems; (iv) no empirical, statistical, measurement or apparatus claim is made, and no quantitative precision is invented; and (v) the scope exclusions (advanced branch, free fields, arbitrary distributions, self-force) are explicit. The classical textbook treatments listed in the sources present the retarded/advanced distinction and the extra choice of the retarded Green function (Tong's 'extra choice' at the displayed page); they support the formulation and the honest status, and are not evidence for the physical correctness of the choice.

before.title: The microscopic vacuum Maxwell equations: smooth and weak branches
before.statement:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on $I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let $\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as distributional derivatives, and let $\psi$ range over $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the pairings $\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$ vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). (c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of inertial frame.
before.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. Obligations and conventions: the fields and sources are those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], the operators are the published divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the weak reading uses exactly the regular-distribution embedding, the test space and the distributional derivative named in the statement. The exposition must state that the four equations are adopted, that the choice of the sign and constant conventions is the one fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]], and that no magnetic charge is included; the sources not covered by either branch are excluded explicitly. Empirical support for Maxwell's equations is a nonlogical relation of the framework, not a proof, and no verification is claimed here.

before.title: Charge continuity as a compatibility condition of the Maxwell equations
before.statement:
Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants and units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $E,B$ be the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], with $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$.

(a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ on $\Omega\times I$ and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$, and suppose the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] holds with these fields and sources, in particular $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. Then the continuity equation
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
holds pointwise on $\Omega\times I$, where $\operatorname{div}$ is the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and $\partial_t$ the partial time derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]].

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be distributions on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); in particular they may be locally integrable fields and sources identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Suppose the four equations
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$ with distributional derivatives. This includes the original locally integrable weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the separately adopted declared singular-source models of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], when their source/field hypotheses hold. More generally the formal compatibility implication applies to every distributional source pair for which the four identities hold, without asserting physical adoption of arbitrary distributions. Then
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$.

The conclusion is a compatibility condition: it does not assert that every source pair is compatible with the Maxwell equations, and by itself it proves no conservation of physical charge. The derivative compatibility argument is choice-free. An application to the declared singular-source model retains the Countable Choice assumption of its defining source/surface-measure formulation ([[def-countable-choice]]).
before.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. By [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] applied to the $C^2$ field $B$, $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$ pointwise. Taking the divergence of the displayed Amp\`ere equation and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives in the sum defining the divergence ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)$, and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] lets the two coordinate-derivative types be interchanged: $\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)=\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)$. The Gauss law of the smooth branch gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$, using $\rho$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substituting, $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=\mu_0(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)$, because $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ by the definition $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\mu_0>0$; division by $\mu_0$ gives the claim.

(b) Distributional branch. Only the two pairings with $\operatorname{curl}B$ and with $\operatorname{div}E$ are used. By [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] the distributional derivatives commute, so for every test function $\psi$
$$\langle\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B),\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_i\partial_jB_k,\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_j\partial_iB_k,\psi\rangle=0$$
after reindexing $i\leftrightarrow j$ and using the antisymmetry of $\varepsilon_{ijk}$: the two expressions are negatives of each other. The weak Amp\`ere equation therefore gives $\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$, again by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] and linearity of the pairing ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). The weak Gauss law gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$; substituting and dividing as in (a) gives $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. The locally integrable case is clause (a) of the embedding: the fields' regular distributions are well defined ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]), and the computation is unchanged. Every step is either an identity for distributions or the definition of the distributional derivative applied to a constant multiple, so no choice principle and no convergence theorem is used. The statement does not claim that every source pair admits fields satisfying the four equations: it claims only that whenever they do, continuity follows. Actual physical use with point/stationary-sheet source models invokes [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], not an extension inferred from the old L1-only postulate. The formal distributional cancellation itself remains choice-free; the source-object formulation retains its explicit Countable Choice assumption.

(b) [Distributional branch] Let $E,B,\rho,J$ be distributions on $\Omega\times I$ ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]); in particular they may be locally integrable fields and sources identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Suppose the four equations
$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$$
hold in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$ with distributional derivatives. This includes the original locally integrable weak branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the separately adopted declared singular-source models of [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], when their source/field hypotheses hold. More generally the formal compatibility implication applies to every distributional source pair for which the four identities hold, without asserting physical adoption of arbitrary distributions. Then
$$\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$$
in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$.

The conclusion is a compatibility condition: it does not assert that every source pair is compatible with the Maxwell equations, and by itself it proves no conservation of physical charge. The derivative compatibility argument is choice-free. An application to the declared singular-source model retains the Countable Choice assumption of its defining source/surface-measure formulation ([[def-countable-choice]]).
used_after.strategy:
(a) Smooth branch. By [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] applied to the $C^2$ field $B$, $\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B)=0$ pointwise. Taking the divergence of the displayed Amp\`ere equation and using linearity of the coordinate derivatives in the sum defining the divergence ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]) gives $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)$, and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]] lets the two coordinate-derivative types be interchanged: $\operatorname{div}(\partial_tE)=\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)$. The Gauss law of the smooth branch gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t(\operatorname{div}E)=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$, using $\rho$ of class $C^1$ ([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]). Substituting, $0=\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho=\mu_0(\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho)$, because $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ by the definition $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]] and $\mu_0>0$; division by $\mu_0$ gives the claim.

(b) Distributional branch. Only the two pairings with $\operatorname{curl}B$ and with $\operatorname{div}E$ are used. By [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] the distributional derivatives commute, so for every test function $\psi$
$$\langle\operatorname{div}(\operatorname{curl}B),\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_i\partial_jB_k,\psi\rangle=\sum_{i,j,k=1}^3\varepsilon_{ijk}\langle\partial_j\partial_iB_k,\psi\rangle=0$$
after reindexing $i\leftrightarrow j$ and using the antisymmetry of $\varepsilon_{ijk}$: the two expressions are negatives of each other. The weak Amp\`ere equation therefore gives $\mu_0\operatorname{div}J+c^{-2}\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$, again by [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]] and linearity of the pairing ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]). The weak Gauss law gives $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and hence $\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\varepsilon_0^{-1}\partial_t\rho$; substituting and dividing as in (a) gives $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in $\mathcal D'(\Omega\times I)$. The locally integrable case is clause (a) of the embedding: the fields' regular distributions are well defined ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]), and the computation is unchanged. Every step is either an identity for distributions or the definition of the distributional derivative applied to a constant multiple, so no choice principle and no convergence theorem is used. The statement does not claim that every source pair admits fields satisfying the four equations: it claims only that whenever they do, continuity follows. Actual physical use with point/stationary-sheet source models invokes [[post-em-distributional-vacuum-maxwell]], not an extension inferred from the old L1-only postulate. The formal distributional cancellation itself remains choice-free; the source-object formulation retains its explicit Countable Choice assumption.

before.title: Controlled electric-dipole far field and retarded-time radiated power of a compact smooth source
before.statement: Assume the setting and hypotheses of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by its suppliers: $c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $a>0$, $t_0<T$, jointly $C^\infty$ fields $\rho,J$ vanishing outside $\overline B_a(0)\times[t_0,T]$ and satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$; let $\varphi,A$ be the retarded potentials and $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ the fields, with $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Adopt the causal selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]]: these retarded fields are the fields of the source model (the compact smooth instance established by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]). Define the **time-dependent electric dipole moment** $$p(u):=\int_{B_a}y\,\rho(y,u)\,dy\in\mathbb R^3$$ (componentwise, about the fixed chart origin of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]; it is the fixed-time analogue of the static source moment of [[def-em-electric-moments]]), and, as in the asymptotic theorem, $I(n,u):=\int_{B_a}J(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$, $V(n,u):=\partial_uI(n,u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)\,dy$ and $$D(u):=\frac{a}{c}\int_{B_a}\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|\,dy.$$ Then: (a) [Moment identities] $p\in C^\infty(\mathbb R;\mathbb R^3)$, $p'(u)=\int_{B_a}J(y,u)\,dy$, $p''(u)=\int_{B_a}J_t(y,u)\,dy$, $\int_{B_a}\rho_t(y,u)\,dy=0$ and the total charge $\int_{B_a}\rho(y,u)\,dy$ vanishes for every $u$. (b) [Dipole replacement error] $|V(n,u)-p''(u)|\le D(u)$ for every $n\in S^2$ and every $u\in[t_0,T]$: the explicit absolute error of the dipole approximation to the source's transverse current moment. (c) [Leading fields] With $\Gamma_E$, $\Gamma_B$ the constants of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](b) (depending only on $a,c,\mu_0$ and the listed source suprema), for every $n\in S^2$, $u\in[t_0,T]$, $r\ge2a$: $$\Bigl|E\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{\mu_0}{4\pi r}n\times(n\times p''(u))\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_E}{r^2}+\frac{\mu_0D(u)}{4\pi r},\qquad \Bigl|B\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)-\frac{n\times E(rn,u+\tfrac rc)}{c}\Bigr|\le\frac{\Gamma_B}{r^2}.$$ The leading far field is the electric-dipole field, with amplitude proportional to $p''(u)$; all errors are uniform in the direction $n$ at fixed $u$. (d) [Retarded-time radiated power] The limit of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]](c) equals $\mu_0|p''(u)|^2/(6\pi c)+R(u)$ with the explicit absolute error $$|R(u)|\le\frac{\mu_0\bigl(2|p''(u)|D(u)+D(u)^2\bigr)}{4\pi c},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}r^2n\cdot S\bigl(rn,u+\tfrac rc\bigr)d\sigma=\frac{\mu_0}{6\pi c}|p''(u)|^2\ \text{ exactly when } D(u)=0.$$ The evaluation uses the sphere moment $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$ of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](d). The limit is at fixed retarded time $u$, not at fixed observation time. (e) [Scope] The compact smooth source branch only; the dipole error is absolute and explicitly controlled by $D(u)$, and no assertion is made that slow or 'nonrelativistic' source motion alone makes $D(u)$ small -- that is a hypothesis on the source's time variation. No point charge, no moving point source, no radiation reaction, no self-force and no empirical or measurement content; the failure of the correspondence with an oscillator for rapidly varying sources is retained through $D(u)$.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]]. (a) $\rho$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, so $u\mapsto p(u)$ is $C^\infty$ by differentiation under the integral sign ([[lem-em-parameter-integrals]]) and $p'(u)=\int y\,\rho_t(y,u)dy$; integrating by parts componentwise over a ball containing the support via the divergence theorem ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]], boundary term zero by compact support) gives $\int y_i\partial_t\rho\,dy=-\int y_i\operatorname{div}J\,dy=\int J_i\,dy$, since $\partial_i(y_iJ_k)$ contributes $J_i$ and the remaining divergence term integrates to zero. Replacing $J$ by $J_t$ (equivalently differentiating in $u$ under the integral sign) gives $p''=\int J_t$. The vanishing $\int\rho_t=0$ is the same divergence theorem with weight $1$ (equivalently clause (f) of [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]]), and the total charge vanishes because $\rho$ is supported in $t\in[t_0,T]$. (b) For fixed $y\in B_a$ the one-variable function $v\mapsto J_t(y,v)$ is $C^1$ on the interval between $u$ and $u+n\cdot y/c$, whose length is at most $a/c$; the mean value theorem ([[cor-mean-value-theorem]]) gives $|J_t(y,u+n\cdot y/c)-J_t(y,u)|\le(a/c)\sup_{|v-u|\le a/c}|J_{tt}(y,v)|$ componentwise, and integrating over $B_a$ with the integral triangle inequality and monotonicity ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]) gives (b). (c) Clause (b) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] writes $E(rn,u+r/c)=E_{\mathrm{lead}}(n,u,r)+$ remainder with $E_{\mathrm{lead}}=\mu_0\,n\times(n\times V(n,u))/(4\pi r)$ and remainder $O(r^{-2})$ bounded by $\Gamma_E r^{-2}$. Substituting $V=p''+(V-p'')$ and using $|n\times(n\times w)|\le|w|$ ([[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]]) gives the first bound; the displayed $B$ bound is the supplier's. (d) By clause (c) of [[thm-em-radiation-asymptotic-flux]] the limit equals $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\int_{S^2}|n\times V|^2d\sigma$. Replacing $V$ by $p''$ changes the integrand by at most $(2|p''|D+D^2)$ pointwise (expand $|n\times V|^2-|n\times p''|^2$ and use the bound (b), the linearity of the cross product and the integral triangle inequality), so the integral changes by at most $4\pi(2|p''|D+D^2)$ and the limit by $\mu_0(2|p''|D+D^2)/(4\pi c)$. The exact dipole value uses $|n\times p''|^2=|p''|^2-(n\cdot p'')^2$ and clause (d) of [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]]: $\int_{S^2}|n\times p''|^2d\sigma=4\pi|p''|^2-(4\pi/3)|p''|^2=(8\pi/3)|p''|^2$, and $\mu_0/(16\pi^2c)\cdot(8\pi/3)=\mu_0/(6\pi c)$. (e) records that the error coefficient $D(u)$ constrains the source's own time variation and that the limit is a fixed-retarded-time limit, as in the supplier; no self-force, point-source, decay or empirical claim is added.
before.physical_scope: Far-zone electric-dipole radiation of a prescribed smooth conserved source of compact spatial support and compact time support: the dipole moment identities, the explicit absolute dipole-replacement error $D(u)$, the uniform leading far fields and the retarded-time radiated power with its absolute error. Excluded: point charges; sources without the compact smooth branch; claims that slowness alone controls $D(u)$; observation-time power and signal-speed readings; self-force, radiation reaction and every empirical or measurement claim.

before.title: Instantaneous-rest Larmor power of a prescribed point charge
before.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], let $q\in\mathbb R$, let $z,v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline, $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), let $s_0$ be an emission event with $z'(s_0)=0$ (the charge is momentarily at rest in the laboratory chart), and put $a:=z''(s_0)$ and, for $n\in S^2$, $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$. Let $E,B$ be the retarded fields of the charge given by [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]] and $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]], [[pthm-em-poynting-balance]]). Then: (a) [Field on the emitted sphere] For every $r>0$ and $n\in S^2$, $$E(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C\,n\times(n\times a)}{c^2r}+\rho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C|\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)=\frac{n\times E(x_r,t_r)}{c}.$$ (b) [Angular flux density] The limits $$\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n):=\lim_{r\to\infty}r^2\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C^{2}\,|n\times(n\times a)|^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}},\qquad P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\int_{S^2}\frac{dP}{d\sigma}(n)\,d\sigma(n),$$ exist with the convergence uniform in $n\in S^2$; $d\sigma$ is the polar surface measure of the unit sphere (equal to the chart surface measure by [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). (c) [Total power] $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\cdot\frac{8\pi}{3}|a|^{2}=\frac{q^2|a|^2}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ the Larmor power of the momentarily resting prescribed charge. If $a=0$ all displayed radiation quantities vanish. (e) [Scope and conventions] The result is exact at an emission event at which the charge is instantaneously at rest in the laboratory chart: then $\kappa_0(n)=1$ for every $n$, so no retarded-time conversion factor appears and the displayed limits are simultaneously the fixed-sphere flux and the emitted power per unit emission time. The prescribed curve, the uniform subluminal bound and $z'(s_0)=0$ are hypotheses; for a varying-velocity worldline the instantaneous rest event is a single parameter value, not an interval.

before.title: Relativistic emitted power of a prescribed point charge at a general emission event
before.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the setting be that of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]]: a charge $q\in\mathbb R$ ($C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$) on a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline $z$ in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], with retarded fields $E,B$ off the worldline and the uniform far-zone remainder of that item; let $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]). Let $s_0$ be an emission event, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\gamma_0:=(1-|\beta_0|^2)^{-1/2}$, $a:=z''(s_0)$, and for $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\kappa_0(n):=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Define the **emitted power at the emission event $s_0$** by the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}\kappa_0(n)\,r^{2}\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)\,d\sigma(n),$$ $d\sigma$ the polar surface measure (equal to the chart surface measure). The weight $\kappa_0$ is the emission-time/observation-time conversion factor of the retarded root, $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$, equivalently the moving-boundary correction $S\cdot n-(z'\cdot n)u$ at leading radiation order, where $u=|S|/c$ for the transverse far field. Then: (a) [Weighted flux limit] The limit exists and $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}\frac{\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}}{\kappa_0(n)^{5}}\,d\sigma(n).$$ (b) [Closed form and four-acceleration form] If $b:=|\beta_0|<1$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp$ is decomposed along $\beta_0=|\beta_0|e_3$ and perpendicular to it, then $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{q^{2}\gamma_0^{6}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)=\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\,\eta(A,A),$$ where $A$ is the four-acceleration of the worldline at $s_0$ and $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](e)). At $\beta_0=0$ the weight is $1$ and (b) reduces to the instantaneous-rest Larmor power of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) [Low-speed comparison] For every $\delta\in(0,1)$ and every emission event with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$, $$\frac{(1-\delta^{2})^{-2}q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)\le\frac{(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \Bigl|P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)-\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\Bigr|\le\frac{3\delta^{2}}{(1-\delta^{2})^{3}}\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ a comparison uniform over the events with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. In particular the instantaneous-rest formula is the exact $\delta=0$ case, and no term of the comparison is asserted to be small without the explicit hypothesis $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. (d) [Scope] $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$ is the power emitted at the single retarded event $s_0$ per unit emission time, defined by the weighted far-zone flux; it is not a coordinate-time loss rate of a dynamical particle, and no dynamics (self-force, radiation reaction, mass), no uniformity in $s_0$, and no empirical or measurement claim is made. The near fields are $O(r^{-2})$ with their uniform remainder as in [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]](c), so their contribution to the weighted $r^2$ flux vanishes; the $\kappa_0$-weighting is part of the definition of emitted power and is not an additional physical assumption.
before.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) On the emitted sphere the retarded data are those of the emission event ($s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]](d)), and the uniform remainder gives $E= E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}+\rho_E$ with $E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)/(c\kappa_0^{3}r)$, $|\rho_E|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ and $B=n\times E/c$. For such fields $n\cdot S=|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)$ (expand $E\times(n\times E/c)$ and use the triple-product orthogonality, [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Therefore $\kappa_0r^{2}n\cdot S=\kappa_0r^{2}|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)=\kappa_0|C|^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}\kappa_0^{6})+O(r^{-1})$ with a remainder controlled by the uniform bound ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]); note $C^{2}=|C|^{2}$ as squares. Integrating over the compact sphere and passing to the limit ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]) gives (a) with $\dot\beta_0=a/c$ absorbed: $|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}$ replaces $c^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}$, giving $(C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5}))\int|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma$ because $|C|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}c^{2})=C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})$ and one power of $\kappa_0$ cancels. (b) Rotate the integration variable so that $\beta_0=be_3$ with $b=|\beta_0|$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp e_1$ (rotation invariance of $\sigma$, [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); put $u=n_3$ and $\kappa_0=1-bu$. Expanding the numerator with $N=n\cdot\beta_0=bu$, $d=n\cdot\dot\beta_0$ and $|n-\beta_0|^{2}=1-2bu+b^{2}$ gives, exactly as in the recorded research computation, $$\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}=-(1-b^{2})(n\cdot a)^{2}+2\kappa_0 b\,a_\parallel(n\cdot a)+\kappa_0^{2}|a|^{2}.$$ Apply [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](b),(c) with $f(u)=(1-bu)^{-5}$ and $g(u)=(1-bu)^{-4}$: the azimuthal average turns $(n\cdot a)^2$ into $u^{2}a_\parallel^{2}+\tfrac12(1-u^{2})a_\perp^{2}$ and $n\cdot a$ into $ua_\parallel$, and $(1-bu)^{-3}$ weights the $|a|^{2}$ term. The resulting one-dimensional integrals are elementary: $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})(1-bu)^{-5}du=\tfrac{4}{3}(1-b^{2})^{-3}$ and $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-bu)^{-3}du=2(1-b^{2})^{-2}$, both verified by the displayed antiderivatives in $y=1-bu$ using the power derivative, chain rule and fundamental theorem ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Collecting terms gives $\int|\cdot|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma=(8\pi/3)[\gamma_0^{6}a_\parallel^{2}+\gamma_0^{4}a_\perp^{2}]= (8\pi/3)\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; multiplying by $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})=q^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ produces (b). The four-acceleration identity is clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], where $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_w^{6}(w\cdot a)^{2}/c^{2}$ with $w=z'(s_0)=c\beta_0$ reads $\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; the $\beta_0=0$ case is the statement of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. used_after.title: Relativistic emitted power of a prescribed point charge at a general emission event
used_after.statement: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as carried by the cited point-source suppliers. Let the setting be that of [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]]: a charge $q\in\mathbb R$ ($C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$) on a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline $z$ in the laboratory chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], with retarded fields $E,B$ off the worldline and the uniform far-zone remainder of that item; let $S:=E\times B/\mu_0$ ([[def-em-vacuum-energy-flux]]). Let $s_0$ be an emission event, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\gamma_0:=(1-|\beta_0|^2)^{-1/2}$, $a:=z''(s_0)$, and for $n\in S^2$ put $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\kappa_0(n):=1-n\cdot\beta_0$. Define the **emitted power at the emission event $s_0$** by the $\kappa_0$-weighted far-zone flux $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\int_{S^2}\kappa_0(n)\,r^{2}\,n\cdot S(x_r,t_r)\,d\sigma(n),$$ $d\sigma$ the polar surface measure (equal to the chart surface measure). The weight $\kappa_0$ is the emission-time/observation-time conversion factor of the retarded root, $\partial_ts=1/\kappa$, equivalently the moving-boundary correction $S\cdot n-(z'\cdot n)u$ at leading radiation order, where $u=|S|/c$ for the transverse far field. Then: (a) [Weighted flux limit] The limit exists and $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{C^{2}}{\mu_0c^{5}}\int_{S^2}\frac{\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}}{\kappa_0(n)^{5}}\,d\sigma(n).$$ (b) [Closed form and four-acceleration form] If $b:=|\beta_0|<1$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp$ is decomposed along $\beta_0=|\beta_0|e_3$ and perpendicular to it, then $$P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)=\frac{q^{2}\gamma_0^{6}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\bigl(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2}\bigr)=\frac{q^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\,\eta(A,A),$$ where $A$ is the four-acceleration of the worldline at $s_0$ and $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$ ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]](e)). At $\beta_0=0$ the weight is $1$ and (b) reduces to the instantaneous-rest Larmor power of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) [Low-speed comparison] For every $\delta\in(0,1)$ and every emission event with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$, $$\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\le P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)\le\frac{(1-\delta^{2})^{-3}q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},\qquad\text{hence}\qquad \Bigl|P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)-\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}}\Bigr|\le\frac{3\delta^{2}}{(1-\delta^{2})^{3}}\frac{q^{2}|a|^{2}}{6\pi\varepsilon_0c^{3}},$$ a comparison uniform over the events with $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. In particular the instantaneous-rest formula is the exact $\delta=0$ case, and no term of the comparison is asserted to be small without the explicit hypothesis $|\beta_0|\le\delta$. (d) [Scope] $P_{\mathrm{em}}(s_0)$ is the power emitted at the single retarded event $s_0$ per unit emission time, defined by the weighted far-zone flux; it is not a coordinate-time loss rate of a dynamical particle, and no dynamics (self-force, radiation reaction, mass), no uniformity in $s_0$, and no empirical or measurement claim is made. The near fields are $O(r^{-2})$ with their uniform remainder as in [[pthm-em-lienard-wiechert]](c), so their contribution to the weighted $r^2$ flux vanishes; the $\kappa_0$-weighting is part of the definition of emitted power and is not an additional physical assumption.
used_after.strategy: Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. (a) On the emitted sphere the retarded data are those of the emission event ($s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, [[thm-em-retarded-root-and-fields]](d)), and the uniform remainder gives $E= E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}+\rho_E$ with $E_{\mathrm{acc,lead}}=C\,n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)/(c\kappa_0^{3}r)$, $|\rho_E|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$ and $B=n\times E/c$. For such fields $n\cdot S=|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)$ (expand $E\times(n\times E/c)$ and use the triple-product orthogonality, [[lem-cross-product-is-bilinear-alternating-and-orthogonal]], [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]). Therefore $\kappa_0r^{2}n\cdot S=\kappa_0r^{2}|n\times E|^{2}/(\mu_0c)=\kappa_0|C|^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}\kappa_0^{6})+O(r^{-1})$ with a remainder controlled by the uniform bound ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]]); note $C^{2}=|C|^{2}$ as squares. Integrating over the compact sphere and passing to the limit ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]) gives (a) with $\dot\beta_0=a/c$ absorbed: $|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}$ replaces $c^{2}|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0)|^{2}$, giving $(C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5}))\int|n\times((n-\beta_0)\times a)|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma$ because $|C|^{2}/(\mu_0c^{3}c^{2})=C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})$ and one power of $\kappa_0$ cancels. (b) Rotate the integration variable so that $\beta_0=be_3$ with $b=|\beta_0|$ and $a=a_\parallel e_3+a_\perp e_1$ (rotation invariance of $\sigma$, [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]); put $u=n_3$ and $\kappa_0=1-bu$. Expanding the numerator with $N=n\cdot\beta_0=bu$, $d=n\cdot\dot\beta_0$ and $|n-\beta_0|^{2}=1-2bu+b^{2}$ gives, exactly as in the recorded research computation, $$\bigl|n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times a\bigr)\bigr|^{2}=-(1-b^{2})(n\cdot a)^{2}+2\kappa_0 b\,a_\parallel(n\cdot a)+\kappa_0^{2}|a|^{2}.$$ Apply [[lem-em-sphere-zonal-moments]](b),(c) with $f(u)=(1-bu)^{-5}$ and $g(u)=(1-bu)^{-4}$: the azimuthal average turns $(n\cdot a)^2$ into $u^{2}a_\parallel^{2}+\tfrac12(1-u^{2})a_\perp^{2}$ and $n\cdot a$ into $ua_\parallel$, and $(1-bu)^{-3}$ weights the $|a|^{2}$ term. The resulting one-dimensional integrals are elementary: $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-u^{2})(1-bu)^{-5}du=\tfrac{4}{3}(1-b^{2})^{-3}$ and $\int_{-1}^{1}(1-bu)^{-3}du=2(1-b^{2})^{-2}$, both verified by the displayed antiderivatives in $y=1-bu$ using the power derivative, chain rule and fundamental theorem ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-ftc-second-part]], [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). Collecting terms gives $\int|\cdot|^{2}/\kappa_0^{5}d\sigma=(8\pi/3)[\gamma_0^{6}a_\parallel^{2}+\gamma_0^{4}a_\perp^{2}]= (8\pi/3)\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; multiplying by $C^{2}/(\mu_0c^{5})=q^{2}/(16\pi^{2}\varepsilon_0c^{3})$ produces (b). The four-acceleration identity is clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], where $\eta(A,A)=\gamma_w^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_w^{6}(w\cdot a)^{2}/c^{2}$ with $w=z'(s_0)=c\beta_0$ reads $\gamma_0^{4}|a|^{2}+\gamma_0^{6}(\beta_0\cdot a)^{2}=\gamma_0^{6}(|a|^{2}-|\beta_0\times a|^{2})$; the $\beta_0=0$ case is the statement of [[pthm-em-larmor-nonrelativistic]]. (c) The strongest immediate eventwise bounds are gamma0^4 P_L<=P_em<=gamma0^6 P_L, since |a|²-|beta0 cross a|² lies between (1-b²)|a|² and |a|². With b<=delta, gamma0>=1 and gamma0^6<=(1-delta²)^-3, they imply P_L<=P_em<=(1-delta²)^-3 P_L. A larger inverse factor in the UNIFORM lower bound is not justified by an upper bound on b (the rest event b0 disproves it). The rational identity (1-delta²)^-3-1=(3delta²-3delta^4+delta^6)/(1-delta²)^3<=3delta²/(1-delta²)^3 proves the unchanged difference estimate, including P_L0. (d) records that the definition is per unit emission time, that the near-field contribution vanishes after weighting by the uniform remainder and that no dynamics or empirical content is added. To make the finite angular integration fully explicit: the parallel averaged numerator is1-u²; the perpendicular one is(1-bu)²-(1-b²)(1-u²)/2. For b>0 the first transformed antiderivative is b^-3[(1-b²)y^-4/4-2y^-3/3+y^-2/2], y=1-bu, evaluated from1-b to1+b. At b0 direct angular moments give8pi|a|²/3; never evaluate a b^-3 antiderivative at b0. The angle-axis rotation preserves the existing sphere measure.

before.title: Retarded point fields off the worldline: Lienard-Wiechert potentials, the velocity/acceleration split and the uniform far-zone remainder
before.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the point-source change-of-variables suppliers below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let the laboratory region, chart and units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]] ($c>0$, $\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$), let $q\in\mathbb R$ and let $z$, $v_*$ be a retarded point-geometry datum of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]] (a prescribed $C^3$ uniformly subluminal worldline of a point charge, [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], with the constants $C:=q/(4\pi\varepsilon_0)$), and let $\rho,J$ be the point-source distributions of that charge on the worldline in the declared point-source class of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) (the $C^3$ branch of the point-current construction). Let $(\varphi,A)$ be the retarded history pairings of [[lem-em-point-retarded-potential-and-fields]](b) -- the framework's retarded construction for this source under the adopted selection [[post-em-radiation-selection]] -- and define $E:=-\nabla\varphi-\partial_tA$, $B:=\nabla\times A$ on the off-worldline domain $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-em-fields]]). Then: (a) [Potentials] $\varphi=C/(\kappa r)$ and $A=\beta\varphi/c$ on $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, where $r,\kappa,\beta$ are the retarded data of [[def-em-retarded-point-geometry]](b); the zero extensions of $\varphi,A$ to $\Gamma$ are locally integrable on $\Omega$. (b) [Exact fields] On $\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $$E=E_{\mathrm{vel}}+E_{\mathrm{acc}},\qquad E_{\mathrm{vel}}=\frac{C(1-|\beta|^2)(n-\beta)}{\kappa^3r^2},\qquad E_{\mathrm{acc}}=\frac{C\,n\times\bigl((n-\beta)\times\dot\beta\bigr)}{c\,\kappa^3r},\qquad B=\frac{n\times E}{c},$$ and $E,B$ are of class $C^1$ there; the velocity part obeys $|E_{\mathrm{vel}}|\le|C|(1+v_*/c)(1-v_*/c)^{-3}r^{-2}$. (c) [Uniform far-zone remainder] For every emission event $s_0$ and direction $n\in S^2$, with $x_r:=z(s_0)+rn$, $t_r:=s_0+r/c$, $\beta_0:=z'(s_0)/c$, $\dot\beta_0:=z''(s_0)/c$ and $\kappa_0:=1-n\cdot\beta_0$: $(x_r,t_r)\in\Omega\setminus\Gamma$, $s(x_r,t_r)=s_0$, and $$E(x_r,t_r)=\frac{C\,n\times\bigl((n-\beta_0)\times\dot\beta_0\bigr)}{c\,\kappa_0^3\,r}+\rho_E(s_0,n,r),\qquad|\rho_E(s_0,n,r)|\le|C|\frac{1+v_*/c}{(1-v_*/c)^3}\,r^{-2},\qquad B(x_r,t_r)=\frac{n\times E(x_r,t_r)}{c};$$ the bound is uniform in $n$ at fixed $s_0$. (d) [Scope] These are the stipulated retarded model fields of the prescribed charge: the item identifies, through the same adopted causal selection used by [[pthm-em-retarded-potentials]] for the compact branch, the point-source potentials and fields of the model, and proves their exact form and bounds. It asserts no value of the fields on the worldline $\Gamma$ (where the formulas are undefined and the self-field is singular), no solution property of the distributional Maxwell system, no integral or energy statement, no self-force and no radiation reaction, and derives no mass. The uniform bound $v_*<c$ and the exclusion of $\Gamma$ are essential hypotheses; the companion example page shows that a merely pointwise subluminal curve can fail to have a retarded root, and no uniformity in the emission event $s_0$ is claimed ($z''$ is not assumed bounded). The signed constant $C$ is retained in every displayed formula while absolute-value bounds use $|C|$.

before.title: Maxwell's equations in potential form: the Lorenz divergence, the decoupled wave equations and residual generators
before.design_state: complete-exact-conditional-research-argument; the exact algebraic identities are stated with their pointwise-regularity hypotheses; solvability is left to the reachability theorem
before.statement:
Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ an interval, $c>0$, and let $(\varphi,A)$ be a potential pair of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-potential-gauge-and-field-conventions]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) with field pair $(E,B)$ ([[def-em-fields]]) and Lorenz divergence and wave operator $$G:=\operatorname{div}A+c^{-2}\partial_t\varphi,\qquad W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta.$$ Let $ho:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R$ and $J:\Omega	imes I	o\mathbb R^3$ be continuous sources ([[def-em-sources]]). (a) [Exact identities] Independently of any field equation, on $\Omega	imes I$ $$\operatorname{div}E=W\varphi-\partial_tG,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=WA+
abla G.$$ Consequently the sourced Maxwell equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] hold for $(E,B,ho,J)$ if and only if $$W\varphi-\partial_tG= rac{ho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad WA+
abla G=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$ (b) [Gauge shift] If $\chi$ is a gauge function of class $C^2$ jointly on $\Omega	imes I$, then $G(T_\chi(\varphi,A))=G-W\chi$ on $\Omega	imes I$ ([[def-em-gauge-transformation]]), and the transformed pair has the same field pair $(E,B)$ ([[pthm-em-gauge-invariance]]). Hence $T_\chi(\varphi,A)$ is in Lorenz gauge if and only if $W\chi=G$ on $\Omega	imes I$. (c) [Decoupling in Lorenz gauge] Suppose additionally that the given potential pair is in Lorenz gauge, $G=0$ on $\Omega	imes I$. Then its field pair solves the sourced Maxwell system of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] if and only if the pair satisfies the decoupled sourced wave equations
$$W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad WA=\mu_0J\qquad	ext{on }\Omega	imes I.$$
The source-free equations $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ are automatic for a potential pair. For an arbitrary given $C^2$ potential pair, the conjunction of Lorenz gauge and these wave equations implies the sourced Maxwell system, but Maxwell's equations alone do not impose $G=0$ on that representative. In full generality their exact equivalent conditions remain the residual equations in (a), including $-\partial_tG$ and $
abla G$. Thus the equivalence with decoupled waves holds within the declared Lorenz gauge, without asserting gauge reachability. (d) [Residual generators] If $W\chi=0$ then the transform of a pair in Lorenz gauge is again in Lorenz gauge with the same field pair; the Lorenz condition therefore does not determine the potential pair. (e) [Scope] The identities and equivalences are properties of a given potential representation of class $C^2$; they assert no existence of a generator with $W\chi=G$ (or with prescribed data), which is the subject of the gauge-reachability theorem on this page, and they impose no boundary, decay or initial condition. A pair of class $C^1$ defines $E,B$ but need not have the second derivatives appearing in $W\varphi$, $WA$, $\Delta$ or $\partial_tG$, so $C^2$ is the exact standing regularity here.

abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A$ for the $C^2$ field $A$ ([[cor-the-curl-of-a-curl-of-a-c2-field]]), the definition $\Delta\varphi=\operatorname{div}
abla\varphi$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]) and the equality of mixed partials of the $C^2$ functions $\varphi,A$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]): $\operatorname{div}E=-\Delta\varphi-\partial_t\operatorname{div}A=W\varphi-\partial_tG$, and $\operatorname{curl}B-c^{-2}\partial_tE=\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=
abla\operatorname{div}A-\Delta A+c^{-2}\partial_t
abla\varphi+c^{-2}\partial_t^2A=WA+
abla G$. The two source-free equations hold automatically for a potential pair by [[thm-the-divergence-of-a-curl-vanishes]] and [[thm-the-curl-of-a-gradient-vanishes]] with the linearity of curl ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]); hence the equivalence with the sourced system. (c) Under the explicitly imposed hypothesis $G=0$, the continuously defined derivatives $\partial_tG$ and $
abla G$ vanish. Substitution in (a) turns the two sourced residual equations exactly into $W\varphi=ho/\varepsilon_0$ and $WA=\mu_0J$. Conversely those two wave equations with $G=0$ make the residual equations hold, and the two source-free equations were already proved for every potential pair.
