before.title: The three-dimensional wave Cauchy problem: Kirchhoff representation, uniqueness, domain of dependence and compact support
before.design_state: complete-exact-declared-branch-conditional-research-argument; published imported wave suppliers routed in place of the design's older distributional edge
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), used through the cited published suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $c>0$, $t_0\in\mathbb R$, $T>t_0$, let $a,b\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and let $h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T])$ in the extension sense that $h$ is the restriction of a $C^\infty$ function on $\mathbb R^3\times J$ for some open interval $J\supset[t_0,T]$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Write $W:=c^{-2}\partial_t^2-\Delta$, so that $c^2W=\Box_c$ is the wave operator of speed $c$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]], [[def-wave-equation-cauchy-data-and-wave-speed]]). For $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ and $s\ge0$ let $H_\varphi(x,s):=s\,M_{cs}\varphi(x)$, where $M_r\varphi(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}\varphi(x+rn)\,d\Omega(n)$ is the spherical mean of [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]]. Define, with $s=t-t_0$, $$u(x,t):=\partial_sH_a(x,s)+H_b(x,s)+c^2\int_{t_0}^{t}H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv,\qquad (x,t)\in\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T],$$ where $h(\cdot,v)$ denotes the map $x\mapsto h(x,v)$ and $\partial_sH_a$ is the partial derivative of $H_a$ in its second argument, evaluated at $s=t-t_0$. Then:

(a) $u$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ in the extension sense, $Wu=h$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$ (indeed on the open neighbourhood of the closed time interval on which the extension of $h$ is defined), $u(\cdot,t_0)=a$ and $\partial_tu(\cdot,t_0)=b$.

(b) Uniqueness: every $v\in C^2(\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T])$ in the extension sense with $Wv=h$ on $\mathbb R^3\times(t_0,T)$, $v(\cdot,t_0)=a$ and $\partial_tv(\cdot,t_0)=b$ equals $u$.

(c) Domain of dependence: let $\tilde a,\tilde b\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, $\tilde h\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T])$ and let $\tilde u$ be the corresponding solution. If $\tilde a=a$ and $\tilde b=b$ on the closed ball $\overline B_{c(t_*-t_0)}(x_*)$ and $\tilde h=h$ on the closed backward cone $K(x_*,t_*):=\{(y,v)\in\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,t_*]:|y-x_*|\le c(t_*-v)\}$ ([[def-forward-and-backward-wave-cones-domain-of-dependence-and-influence]]), then $\tilde u(x_*,t_*)=u(x_*,t_*)$ for every $x_*\in\mathbb R^3$ and $t_*\in[t_0,T]$.

(d) Compact support: if $a$ vanishes off a compact $K_a\subset\mathbb R^3$, $b$ vanishes off a compact $K_b$, and $h(\cdot,v)$ vanishes off a fixed compact $K_h$ for every $v\in[t_0,T]$, then for every $t\in[t_0,T]$ the function $u(\cdot,t)$ has compact spatial support: if $K_a\cup K_b\cup K_h\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)$ for some $\rho>0$ (which exists, [[thm-heine-borel-rn]]), then $u(x,t)=0$ whenever $|x|>\rho+c(t-t_0)$.

No boundary condition on a finite spatial domain, no finite-total-energy hypothesis, and no decay of $a,b,h$ at infinity is assumed or asserted.
before.strategy:
Time translation $t\mapsto t-t_0$ (chain rule) reduces the proof to $t_0=0$; the operator and the formula are invariant under it. Decompose $u=u_h+u_s$ with $u_h:=\partial_sH_a(x,s)+H_b(x,s)$ and $u_s:=c^2\int_{t_0}^{t}H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$, $s=t-t_0$.

(1) Smoothness. By [[lem-em-spherical-mean-family-smoothness]] the map $(x,s,v)\mapsto M(x,s,v)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+sn,v)\,d\Omega(n)$ is $C^\infty$ jointly, hence so is $(x,t,v)\mapsto H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)=(t-v)M(x,c(t-v),v)$ on the region $t_0\le v\le t\le T$, and for fixed $x$ it is $C^\infty$ near the closed triangle $t_0\le v\le t\le T$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). For the same reason $u_h\in C^\infty$, and for fixed $x$ the integrand $v\mapsto H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)$ is $C^\infty$ on $[t_0,t]$; the fixed-interval clause of [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates $u_s$ in $x$ under the integral sign, and [[lem-derivative-of-an-integral-with-moving-endpoints]] differentiates it in $t$ with the endpoint terms. Iterating these two steps (each differentiated integrand is again $C^\infty$ jointly) gives $u_s\in C^\infty$ and $u\in C^\infty$ in the extension sense.

(2) Equation and initial data. [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]] gives, for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, $\partial_t^2H_\varphi=c^2\Delta H_\varphi$ for $t\ge0$, $H_\varphi(\cdot,0)=0$ and $\partial_tH_\varphi(\cdot,0)=\varphi$. Hence $\partial_t^2(\partial_sH_a)=\partial_s(\partial_t^2H_a)=c^2\Delta\partial_sH_a$ and $\partial_t^2H_b=c^2\Delta H_b$, so $\partial_t^2u_h=c^2\Delta u_h$; here $\partial_s$ commutes with $\Delta$ on $C^\infty$ functions ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and $\Delta$ is linear ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Also $u_h(\cdot,t_0)=a$, $\partial_tu_h(\cdot,t_0)=b$ because $\partial_s^2H_a(\cdot,0)=c^2\Delta H_a(\cdot,0)=0$. For $u_s$, two applications of [[lem-derivative-of-an-integral-with-moving-endpoints]] at fixed $x$ give $\partial_tu_s=c^2\int_{t_0}^t\partial_tH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$ (the endpoint term $H_{h(\cdot,t)}(x,0)$ vanishes) and $\partial_t^2u_s=c^2\bigl[\partial_tH_{h(\cdot,t)}(x,0)+\int_{t_0}^t\partial_t^2H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv\bigr]=c^2h(x,t)+c^2\int_{t_0}^tc^2\Delta_xH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$; differentiating in $x$ under the integral sign with [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] gives $\Delta u_s=c^2\int_{t_0}^t\Delta_xH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$, so $\partial_t^2u_s=c^2h+c^2\Delta u_s$, i.e. $Wu_s=h$. Finally $u_s(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $\partial_tu_s(\cdot,t_0)=0$ because $H_\varphi(\cdot,0)=0$. Adding the two parts gives (a); note the normalisation $c^2W=\Box_c$ is what places the factor $c^2$ on the source integral.

(3) Uniqueness and domain of dependence. If $v$ is a second $C^2$ solution with the same data, then $w:=u-v$ solves $\Box_cw=0$ on a neighbourhood of $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ and has $w(\cdot,t_0)=\partial_tw(\cdot,t_0)=0$. Fix $(x_*,t_*)$ with $t_*>t_0$ and shift time; on the closed backward cone of [[def-forward-and-backward-wave-cones-domain-of-dependence-and-influence]] the functions $w$ and the zero solution satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-domain-of-dependence-and-local-uniqueness]] (zeros agree, and the sources $0$ agree), so $w\equiv0$ on that cone and in particular $w(x_*,t_*)=0$; as $(x_*,t_*)$ is arbitrary, $w=0$. Claim (c) is the same argument applied to $u-\tilde u$, whose data agree on the base ball $\overline B_{c(t_*-t_0)}(x_*)$ and whose source vanishes on the cone.

(4) Compact support. In the displayed formula for $u(x,t)$ each term integrates over spheres of radius $cs$ or $c(t-v)$, $0\le t-v\le t-t_0$, centred at $x$, the integrands being $a,\nabla a,b$ or $h(\cdot,v)$; if $\overline B_{c(t-t_0)}(x)$ does not meet $K:=K_a\cup K_b\cup K_h$, all these integrals vanish and $u(x,t)=0$. If $K\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)$ and $|x|>\rho+c(t-t_0)$, then every $y\in\overline B_{c(t-t_0)}(x)$ has $|y|\ge|x|-c(t-t_0)>\rho$, so $\overline B_{c(t-t_0)}(x)\cap K=\emptyset$ and $u(x,t)=0$; the existence of $\rho$ is the boundedness of the compact set $K$ ([[thm-heine-borel-rn]]), which also gives that $\overline B_{\rho+c(t-t_0)}(0)$ is compact. This proves (d) and completes the proof.

(d) Compact support: if $a$ vanishes off a compact $K_a\subset\mathbb R^3$, $b$ vanishes off a compact $K_b$, and $h(\cdot,v)$ vanishes off a fixed compact $K_h$ for every $v\in[t_0,T]$, then for every $t\in[t_0,T]$ the function $u(\cdot,t)$ has compact spatial support: if $K_a\cup K_b\cup K_h\subseteq\overline B_\rho(0)$ for some $\rho>0$ (which exists, [[thm-heine-borel-rn]]), then $u(x,t)=0$ whenever $|x|>\rho+c(t-t_0)$.

No boundary condition on a finite spatial domain, no finite-total-energy hypothesis, and no decay of $a,b,h$ at infinity is assumed or asserted.
used_after.strategy:
Time translation $t\mapsto t-t_0$ (chain rule) reduces the proof to $t_0=0$; the operator and the formula are invariant under it. Decompose $u=u_h+u_s$ with $u_h:=\partial_sH_a(x,s)+H_b(x,s)$ and $u_s:=c^2\int_{t_0}^{t}H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$, $s=t-t_0$.

(1) Smoothness. By [[lem-em-spherical-mean-family-smoothness]] the map $(x,s,v)\mapsto M(x,s,v)=\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{S^2}h(x+sn,v)\,d\Omega(n)$ is $C^\infty$ jointly, hence so is $(x,t,v)\mapsto H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)=(t-v)M(x,c(t-v),v)$ on the region $t_0\le v\le t\le T$, and for fixed $x$ it is $C^\infty$ near the closed triangle $t_0\le v\le t\le T$ ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]). For the same reason $u_h\in C^\infty$, and for fixed $x$ the integrand $v\mapsto H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)$ is $C^\infty$ on $[t_0,t]$; the fixed-interval clause of [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] differentiates $u_s$ in $x$ under the integral sign, and [[lem-derivative-of-an-integral-with-moving-endpoints]] differentiates it in $t$ with the endpoint terms. Iterating these two steps (each differentiated integrand is again $C^\infty$ jointly) gives $u_s\in C^\infty$ and $u\in C^\infty$ in the extension sense.

(2) Equation and initial data. [[lem-em-spherical-mean-wave-identity]] gives, for every $\varphi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$, $\partial_t^2H_\varphi=c^2\Delta H_\varphi$ for $t\ge0$, $H_\varphi(\cdot,0)=0$ and $\partial_tH_\varphi(\cdot,0)=\varphi$. Hence $\partial_t^2(\partial_sH_a)=\partial_s(\partial_t^2H_a)=c^2\Delta\partial_sH_a$ and $\partial_t^2H_b=c^2\Delta H_b$, so $\partial_t^2u_h=c^2\Delta u_h$; here $\partial_s$ commutes with $\Delta$ on $C^\infty$ functions ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]) and $\Delta$ is linear ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). Also $u_h(\cdot,t_0)=a$, $\partial_tu_h(\cdot,t_0)=b$ because $\partial_s^2H_a(\cdot,0)=c^2\Delta H_a(\cdot,0)=0$. For $u_s$, two applications of [[lem-derivative-of-an-integral-with-moving-endpoints]] at fixed $x$ give $\partial_tu_s=c^2\int_{t_0}^t\partial_tH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$ (the endpoint term $H_{h(\cdot,t)}(x,0)$ vanishes) and $\partial_t^2u_s=c^2\bigl[\partial_tH_{h(\cdot,t)}(x,0)+\int_{t_0}^t\partial_t^2H_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv\bigr]=c^2h(x,t)+c^2\int_{t_0}^tc^2\Delta_xH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$; differentiating in $x$ under the integral sign with [[lem-em-parameter-integrals]] gives $\Delta u_s=c^2\int_{t_0}^t\Delta_xH_{h(\cdot,v)}(x,t-v)\,dv$, so $\partial_t^2u_s=c^2h+c^2\Delta u_s$, i.e. $Wu_s=h$. Finally $u_s(\cdot,t_0)=0$ and $\partial_tu_s(\cdot,t_0)=0$ because $H_\varphi(\cdot,0)=0$. Adding the two parts gives (a); note the normalisation $c^2W=\Box_c$ is what places the factor $c^2$ on the source integral.

(3) Uniqueness and domain of dependence. If $v$ is a second $C^2$ solution with the same data, then $w:=u-v$ solves $\Box_cw=0$ on a neighbourhood of $\mathbb R^3\times[t_0,T]$ and has $w(\cdot,t_0)=\partial_tw(\cdot,t_0)=0$. Fix $(x_*,t_*)$ with $t_*>t_0$ and shift time; on the closed backward cone of [[def-forward-and-backward-wave-cones-domain-of-dependence-and-influence]] the functions $w$ and the zero solution satisfy the hypotheses of [[thm-domain-of-dependence-and-local-uniqueness]] (zeros agree, and the sources $0$ agree), so $w\equiv0$ on that cone and in particular $w(x_*,t_*)=0$; as $(x_*,t_*)$ is arbitrary, $w=0$. Claim (c) is the same argument applied to $u-\tilde u$, whose data agree on the base ball $\overline B_{c(t_*-t_0)}(x_*)$ and whose source vanishes on the cone.

(4) Compact support. In the displayed formula for $u(x,t)$ each term integrates over spheres of radius $cs$ or $c(t-v)$, $0\le t-v\le t-t_0$, centred at $x$, the integrands being $a,\nabla a,b$ or $h(\cdot,v)$; if $\overline B_{c(t-t_0)}(x)$ does not meet $K:=K_a\cup K_b\cup K_h$, all these integrals vanish and $u(x,t)=0$. before.title: Norms of four-velocity and four-acceleration, and the observer rest-space decomposition
before.statement: Let c > 0 and let (A,V,eta,C^+) be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space. (a) Norm of the four-velocity. Let x: I -> A be a C^1 future timelike worldline with four-velocity U (def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration). Then eta(U(s),U(s)) = -c^2 for every s in I; equivalently the dimensionless four-velocity u = U/c satisfies eta(u,u) = -1, and U(s) is future timelike. Thus the four-velocity of a worldline lies on the future unit hyperboloid. (b) Orthogonality of the four-acceleration. If x is C^2 at s, then eta(U(s),A(s)) = 0: the four-acceleration has no component along the four-velocity; if in addition A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) is spacelike. (c) Rest space and projection. Let n in V be future unit timelike, eta(n,n) = -1, and put n^perp := {v in V : eta(n,v) = 0}. Then n^perp is a 3-dimensional linear subspace of V, the restriction of eta to n^perp is positive definite, and the map h: V -> V, h(v) := v + eta(n,v) n, is linear, idempotent with h o h = h, has image n^perp and kernel span(n), satisfies h(n) = 0 and eta(n,h(v)) = 0 for all v in V, and every v in V has the unique decomposition v = -eta(n,v) n + h(v). Moreover |w| := sqrt(eta(w,w)) defines a norm on n^perp. (d) Relative velocity and Lorentz factor. Let n and u be future unit timelike vectors, put gamma := -eta(n,u) and w := c h(u)/gamma. Then gamma >= 1, w lies in n^perp, u = gamma (n + w/c), |w|^2 = c^2 (1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and gamma = 1 if and only if u = n. The vector w is the velocity of a worldline with four-velocity c u relative to the observer n and gamma is its Lorentz factor. (e) Coordinate form. Let (o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3) be an inertial frame and let y be a C^1 future timelike worldline whose inertial coordinates are t |-> (c t, r(t)), with coordinate velocity w(t) := r'(t) in R^3 and, when y is C^2, coordinate acceleration a(t) := w'(t). Then |w(t)| < c, the four-velocity is U = gamma_w (c,w) with gamma_w := (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}, and the four-acceleration is A = gamma_w (d/dt)(gamma_w (c,w)), so that A^0 = gamma_w^4 (w.a)/c and A_vec = gamma_w^2 a + gamma_w^4 (w.a) w/c^2; consequently eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0, with eta(A,A) = 0 if and only if a = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0. For the observer n = e_0 of the chart, clauses (c) and (d) specialize to gamma = gamma_w and w_rel = w. (f) Scope. The statement is a theorem about the affine Minkowski model with a fixed positive constant c; it asserts no clock reading and identifies no physical four-velocity. No choice principle is used.
before.strategy: Proof in dependency order; the hard part is (c), which is pure algebra plus one coordinate computation, and the remaining clauses follow from it. (c) Fix an eta-orthonormal basis with e_0 timelike (lem-lorentz-form-has-orthonormal-basis; use an inertial frame of def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart). Write n = n^0 e_0 + n_s and v = v^0 e_0 + v_s with n_s,v_s in S = span(e_1,e_2,e_3), where eta restricts to the positive definite delta with norm |.| (def-spatial-euclidean-structure-of-an-inertial-frame). From eta(n,n) = -(n^0)^2 + |n_s|^2 = -1 one gets (n^0)^2 = 1 + |n_s|^2 > 0. For v with eta(n,v) = -n^0 v^0 + delta(n_s,v_s) = 0 one has v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0, hence eta(v,v) = -(v^0)^2 + |v_s|^2 = |v_s|^2 - delta(n_s,v_s)^2/(n^0)^2 >= |v_s|^2 (1 - |n_s|^2/(n^0)^2) = |v_s|^2/(n^0)^2 >= 0 by the finite Cauchy-Schwarz inequality for delta (thm-cauchy-schwarz-finite); equality forces |v_s| = 0 and then v^0 = 0, so v = 0 and the restriction is positive definite. The map v_s |-> v^0 e_0 + v_s with v^0 = delta(n_s,v_s)/n^0 is a linear bijection S -> n^perp, so n^perp is 3-dimensional. The properties of h are immediate from bilinearity of eta (def-lorentz-form-and-inertia, def-linear-map): eta(n,h(v)) = eta(n,v) + eta(n,v)eta(n,n) = 0, so h(v) lies in n^perp; h(n) = n + eta(n,n)n = 0; h(h(v)) = h(v) + eta(n,h(v))n = h(v); and v = -eta(n,v)n + h(v) is unique because the two summands lie in span(n) and n^perp, which meet only in 0. (a) By def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration, U = x'/tau' with tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(-eta(x',x')), so eta(U,U) = eta(x',x')/(tau')^2 = eta(x',x') c^2/(-eta(x',x')) = -c^2; timelikeness and the future direction of U follow from those of x' and positivity of 1/tau'. (b) eta(U,U) is the constant -c^2 along a C^2 worldline; differentiating componentwise in an eta-orthonormal basis with thm-algebra-of-derivatives gives 0 = (d/ds) eta(U,U) = 2 eta(U,U'), hence eta(U,U') = 0, and dividing by tau' > 0 gives eta(U,A) = 0. If A(s) is nonzero, then A(s) lies in (U(s)/c)^perp, a positive definite space by (c), so eta(A,A) > 0: A(s) is spacelike. (d) By (c), h(u) lies in n^perp and u = gamma n + h(u) with gamma = -eta(n,u). First, gamma > 0: in the inertial frame of (c), future timelikeness of n and u gives n^0 > |n_s| and u^0 > |u_s| (lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components), so eta(n,u) = -n^0 u^0 + delta(n_s,u_s) <= -n^0 u^0 + |n_s||u_s| < 0. Second, eta(u,u) = gamma^2 eta(n,n) + eta(h(u),h(u)) = -gamma^2 + |h(u)|^2 = -1, so |h(u)|^2 = gamma^2 - 1 >= 0, giving gamma >= 1; substituting w = c h(u)/gamma gives |w|^2 = c^2 (gamma^2-1)/gamma^2 = c^2(1 - gamma^{-2}) < c^2, and solving for gamma gives gamma = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{-1/2} and gamma = 1 iff h(u) = 0 iff u = n. (e) In the chart the coordinate path is t |-> (c t, r(t)), so x' = (c,w) and -eta(x',x') = c^2 - |w|^2 > 0 by future timelikeness, giving |w| < c and tau' = c^{-1} sqrt(c^2-|w|^2) = (1 - |w|^2/c^2)^{1/2} = 1/gamma_w; hence U = x'/tau' = gamma_w (c,w). For C^2 paths, d gamma_w/dt = gamma_w^3 (w.a)/c^2 by thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives (applied to the power -1/2) with the chain rule, and collecting terms in A = gamma_w dU/dt gives the displayed components; expanding eta(A,A) in the diagonal form and using gamma_w^2(1-|w|^2/c^2) = 1 gives eta(A,A) = gamma_w^4 |a|^2 + gamma_w^6 (w.a)^2/c^2 >= 0 with equality iff |a| = 0, and eta(U,A) = 0 agrees with (b). (f) The specialization n = e_0 is the evaluation h(u) = u - u^0 e_0 = (0, w/c gamma_w) and gamma = u^0 = gamma_w, so w_rel = w. No choice principle is used; all arguments are finite-dimensional or one-variable calculus.
